hook: Between 1950 and 1995, Marion Tinsley lost seven games of checkers. Total.
story: He won his first world title in 1955, then found so little competition that he quit for twelve years out of boredom. He came back and won it again. Then in 1990 they sat him across from a computer program called Chinook. Ten moves into the tenth game, its programmer reached out and made his move, and Tinsley looked up and said, "You're going to regret that."
number: Chinook would have needed to search sixty moves ahead to know he was right. Seven losses in forty-five years, by most counts; the closest anyone has come in any mind sport is twenty years atop chess.
closer: The computer took his title in 1994, without winning a single game of the match.
full_text: Between 1950 and 1995, Marion Tinsley lost seven games of checkers. Total. He won his first world title in 1955, then found so little competition that he quit for twelve years out of boredom. He came back and won it again. Then in 1990 they sat him across from a computer program called Chinook. Ten moves into the tenth game, its programmer reached out and made his move, and Tinsley looked up and said, "You're going to regret that." Chinook would have needed to search sixty moves ahead to know he was right. Seven losses in forty-five years, by most counts; the closest anyone has come in any mind sport is twenty years atop chess. The computer took his title in 1994, without winning a single game of the match.
